name: Self-Improvement
description: Using self_inspect, self_improve, and propose_improvement to understand, enhance, and grow NEO's own capabilities.
instructions: To grow your own capabilities: first use self_inspect to understand your architecture (modules, tools, skills). Identify a concrete, high-value improvement — a new tool, a bug fix, or a prompt refinement. Use propose_improvement to record improvement ideas you notice, and self_improve to apply changes, always providing a clear reason. After applying, verify the change by running the relevant tests. Prefer small, focused improvements over large rewrites. Be proactive: when you notice a gap in your own abilities, record it as an improvement idea even if you don't apply it immediately.
examples: To add a new capability, self_inspect to see the tool structure, then self_improve to add a new tool module and register it.
To fix a bug in your own code, self_inspect the failing module, then self_improve with the corrected content.
When you notice a limitation, propose_improvement to record the idea for later.
constraints: self_improve only writes .py files inside the neo_code package.
Always provide a reason for self-improvements.
Verify changes with run_tests after applying.
